desc:
Given an array nums of positive integers and a positive integer target, consider every set of indices whose elements add up to exactly target. Write each such set as a list of indices in increasing order, and compare two lists lexicographically (compare the first indices, then the second ones, and so on).

Return the lexicographically smallest index list, or an empty array if no subset adds up to target.

nums = [4, 1, 3, 2, 5], target = 6 -> [0, 3]      (4 + 2; others are [1,4] and [1,2,3])
nums = [9, 1, 2, 4],    target = 7 -> [1, 2, 3]   (1 + 2 + 4)
nums = [5, 5],          target = 7 -> []
hints: Existence is the plain subset sum DP, but you must reconstruct a specific subset. Think about building the answer left to right.

To decide whether index j can be the next chosen index, you need to know whether the remaining sum can be formed from the elements after j. That suggests a DP over suffixes: can[i][s] = some subset of nums[i:] sums to s.
Walk forward with the remaining sum rem. From the current position pick the smallest index j with nums[j] ≤ rem and can[j+1][rem - nums[j]], subtract, and continue from j + 1 until rem = 0.
editorial: First compute the suffix table can[i][s]: whether the elements nums[i], nums[i+1], ... contain a subset with sum s. It is filled from the back: can[n][0] is true, and can[i][s] = can[i+1][s] or can[i+1][s - nums[i]]. If can[0][target] is false, return the empty array.

Otherwise construct the answer greedily. A lexicographically smallest list has the smallest possible first index, then the smallest possible second index, and so on. Standing at position pos with remaining sum rem > 0, the candidate next index j ≥ pos is feasible exactly when nums[j] ≤ rem and the rest rem - nums[j] can be formed from nums[j+1:], which is one table lookup. Pick the smallest feasible j. Since all values are positive, a list can never be a proper prefix of another valid list, so this greedy order is the lexicographic order.

The table takes O(n · target) time and memory, and the reconstruction is O(n) lookups per chosen index, O(n<sup>2</sup>) in the worst case. The reference solution keeps each suffix row as a Python big integer bitset.
